note.saw: An empty canvas and a fish famous for two things: bold black, white and yellow bands, and an impossibly long white streamer trailing from its fin.
note.changing: Lays down the first full structure: a honeycomb vortex of jewel-eyes filling the corners, rings of curled flame petals, the fish with its three bands, the streamer curling into a spiral, and SavesFish lettered along the bottom.
note.why: The bands and the streamer are what make a moorish idol, so they had to become the stars of the trip from the very first sketch.
note.idea: A moorish idol in profile inside a mandala halo: its long white dorsal streamer curls into a spiral of eyes, its bold black, white and yellow bands become psychedelic patterns, and a chrysanthemum of flame petals and compass rings glows behind it.

note.saw: The fish read as a stiff kite with a flat triangular fin and straight edges everywhere, and the big dark spiral looked like a snail shell stuck onto the art.
note.changing: Rebuilds the silhouette with a rounded disc body, a sickle-shaped dorsal fin and a tube snout, curves the bands with the body, gives the scales volume, darkens the petals and sets the name on a dark cartouche.
note.why: The silhouette has to say moorish idol before anything else can work.

note.saw: The streamer ran flat along the rim and merged with the ring of glyphs, and the dark eye band poked up into the dorsal fin as an ugly rectangle.
note.changing: Shrinks the fish slightly for breathing room, trims the eye band so it stops at the body, runs stripes along the edges of the dorsal and anal fins, and spreads the eye's ripple rings across the pale face.
note.why: Giving the halo room around the fish lets both of them read instead of crowding each other.

note.saw: The streamer still looked like a cane handle with a separate dark disc on its end, and the magenta pectoral fin looked like a small fish pasted onto the body.
note.changing: Removes the pectoral fin, wraps the fish in a wide soft halo of light, adds hatch marks and cream cores inside the petals, and starts turning the streamer into a spiral packed with eyes.
note.why: The pasted-on fin had to go, the fish needed to glow against the busy halo, and a spiral that grows from the fin itself feels alive instead of attached.

note.saw: The compass half of the middle-ground style was missing: apart from the rim rings there was no geometry in the halo, the tail was plain, and the whip's outer sweep crowded the rim.
note.changing: Lays an 18-point gold star rosette with jewel nodes over the petals, loosens the spiral so the whip clears the rim, adds stripes inside the tail, and sets a row of runes in the cartouche.
note.why: The middle-ground style needs a geometric skeleton under the freehand ornament.

note.saw: The rune row under the name was too small and faint, half hidden by the letters, and in close-ups the corner jewels were flat inside.
note.changing: Widens the cartouche around a framed gold rune row, gives every corner jewel a second nested bevel and a ring of dots, and stipples the petal bands.
note.why: Detail has to survive a close look, so every part needs something more to find when you lean in.

note.saw: The halo glow and the light from the coil piled up into a pale cyan haze that washed out the right side, and the dorsal fin was the one area with no eyes.
note.changing: Tones the glow down, sets eyes riding along the rays of the dorsal and anal fins, and runs a line of dotted script along the whip.
note.why: Eyes everywhere is the DMT rule, and haze kills colour.

note.saw: In close-up the base of the tail was a flat orange strip, because the scales stopped short of it.
note.changing: Lets the scales run all the way into the tail base; along the way the scale rows and the eyes in the honeycomb band also shifted into new positions across the body.
note.why: No dead zones, even small ones.

note.saw: SavesFish called the old lettering unreadable: small, blobby letters with a heavy pink 3D extrusion sitting over busy fins.
note.changing: Rebuilds the name in big, open letters with a cream fill, gold edge and dark outline, no extrusion, on a larger plain dark cartouche; the fish shrinks and lifts a little so its fins clear the name.
note.why: The name has to read instantly, even as a small thumbnail; style comes second.

note.saw: Sparkles landed on top of the letters, and the new cartouche was a large empty dark field.
note.changing: Moves the sparkles underneath the cartouche and fills it with a dim honeycomb that parts around the letters, leaving a clear margin round each one.
note.why: Nothing empty, but nothing busy touching the name.

note.saw: Fresh eyes on draft 1: the fish read as a kite or a generic angelfish, its biggest shape (the sail) was the emptiest, the halo was wallpaper with no hierarchy, there was no hyperspace depth, and the name sat on a flat panel pasted over the bottom.
note.changing: Nothing yet: the second artist renders the first artist's finished draft unchanged, at full size and in close-ups, to study it before starting over.
note.why: You have to see what is really there, at every size, before deciding what to keep; here the answer was a full rewrite.
note.idea: Let the moorish idol's long white filament become the whole composition: one continuous ribbon that leaves the fin tip, sweeps round the rim, swells into the banner that carries the name and rolls up into a scroll spiral of eyes, while the black bands open into windows onto hyperspace.

note.saw: The scroll spiral had landed right on the fish's snout, the rainbow echo lines along the streamer were too heavy, and the drawing had grown very heavy overall.
note.changing: Rebuilds the spiral so it rolls up out of the banner, down and to the left under the snout, and makes the echo lines thin along the streamer but rich along the banner.
note.why: The scroll should finish the ribbon's gesture in open space rather than collide with the fish, and the streamer should stay a fine line while the banner carries the weight.

note.saw: Twenty-four identical petals at one brightness made the halo busy and flat with no depth, and thin gold star lines read as scratches.
note.changing: Twelve big flame petals in two alternating shapes, twelve cool teal inner petals and eye-spirals in the gaps, with the honeycomb vortex now visible inside the badge around a cream-cyan core of light; the gold star lines are gone.
note.why: A chrysanthemum needs rhythm and layers, big and small, warm and cool, or it turns into wallpaper.

note.saw: The sail was still the calmest field, and nothing in the piece watched back except small eyes.
note.changing: Stacks a totem of three almond-eyed entity faces with jester crowns in the sail, adds rosettes at the ends of the banner and a beaded gold band in the fish's outline; this first pass drew the faces so thickly they came out as white blobs.
note.why: The Idol should carry an idol: DMT space is full of beings that look at you, and a stacked totem suits a fish named after an idol.

note.saw: The aura had become a fog over the petals, and the scroll's channel was too thin to hold its eyes.
note.changing: Softens the aura, makes the honeycomb's lines glow, fattens the scroll's channel with bigger eyes, and gives the tail small eyes and dashed echo lines; the colours of the corner jewels also reshuffle.
note.why: Glow should feel like light coming from inside, not fog.

note.saw: The streamer, the idol's signature, all but vanished at thumbnail size.
note.changing: Widens the streamer along its whole run from the sail round the right side of the rim.
note.why: If the signature line disappears when the piece is small, the fish stops being a moorish idol.

note.saw: The fish now reads as a moorish idol at thumbnail size and the name reads instantly, but the halo burns at one brightness out to the rim, so the idol sits on a flat tapestry; the tail was flat rays with one eye, the scroll a closed shell, and the tunnel ended in plain light.
note.changing: A dark ultraviolet fall-off over the outer halo with the petal eyes glinting out of it, the tail turned into a gate of nested fan outlines round a white-hot pinpoint, gold rays in the scroll, a tiny idol at the end of the tunnel, beads of light down the streamer, hidden machine-elf sigils and glyph bubbles rising from the snout.
note.why: Depth is the breakthrough feeling: a bright core falling away into dark lets the idol float forward, and the same doorway at three sizes, plus a fish waiting inside the fish, is how hyperspace folds into itself.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's dark fall-off, tail gate, scroll rays, tiny idol, travelling beads, machine-elf sigils and glyph bubbles, but turned down re-striping the sail because the totem lives there now.

note.saw: The abyss works and the idol floats forward, but the tiny idol in the tunnel came out as a black four-point star that killed the white-hot core, the scroll's rays ran out over the banner, every eye in the hall stared in a random direction, and the belly seam read like a crack in glass.
note.changing: The tunnel idol turns white with ultraviolet bands against a bigger glow, the scroll rays shorten, every eye outside the fish turns toward the idol's eye, the corner crystals light up from the centre, moire rings shimmer in the gaps under the petals, gold stitches sew the belly seam, chevrons funnel down the snout, and two ghost faces reflect the totem in the black anal fin.
note.why: A temple has one light and everything in it faces that light, so when every eye in the halo turns toward the idol your own gaze is pulled there too.
note.visionary: Took the Visionary's ideas of turning every halo eye toward the idol, lighting the corner crystals from the centre, moire rings in the lit gaps, a stitched belly seam, a chevron funnel on the snout and ghost reflections of the totem in the anal fin.

note.saw: Every eye now turns toward the idol, the corner crystals catch its light and the tiny white idol waits in the tunnel, but the two ghost faces in the anal fin were so faint they read as grey smudges.
note.changing: Raises the ghost faces from 38 to 52 percent strength; nothing else changes before the final check.
note.why: A reflection should be just clear enough to make you look twice; any fainter and it looks like a mistake.

visions.seen: The idol glides out of a honeycomb wormhole with a chrysanthemum for an eye, and a thousand tiny lids on its flanks blink back at me. Every band is an open window into hyperspace now; only the tall cream sail still feels like the daylight world.
suggestions: The tall cream dorsal sail, top center (from the forehead up to the fin tip near x 430, y 60 in the 800 px render, and down its concave trailing edge). It is the biggest and calmest field left: vertical hairlines and dots. I see it as a veil. Keep the cream base so the sail still reads pale at badge size, but swap the vertical hairlines for 7 to 9 thin rainbow contour lines (1.2 to 1.6 px; magenta, orange, gold, green, cyan, violet, repeat). They run parallel to the concave trailing edge and pack tighter toward the tip, each gap about 0.8x the one before, with the little eyes shrinking along with them. The sail then stretches to infinity at its tip, the way hyperspace surfaces drag your gaze to a vanishing point. While you're up there, the streamer could grow out of the tip as a tapering point instead of the squared-off butt joint it makes now.

The black fan tail, far right (around x 660 to 720, y 300 to 420). Right now it's flat blue rays with one small eye. What if it became a little gate: 5 or 6 inset copies of the fan outline shrinking toward the eye (scale about 0.8 each, alternating cyan and violet strokes, opacity falling off inward), with the eye turned into a white-hot pinpoint (radial gradient white to cyan to transparent, r about 6)? Band B's tunnel is the big portal and the scroll's gold jewel is the tiny one. The tail would be the middle one, so one doorway repeats at three scales, and that is exactly how the realm builds itself.

The scroll spiral, lower left above the ribbon's end (around x 115 to 200, y 450 to 520). It shrank since #90, and at 240 px it reads like a snail shell resting on the ribbon. Instead of curling in, let it breathe out: 12 hair-thin gold rays (0.7 px) burst from the gold center jewel across the whorls, clipped to the spiral's own outer stroke, over a soft cyan glow behind the center (radial gradient, r about 30, opacity 0.35). It becomes a portal opening, not a shell, and nothing crosses into the cartouche or near the letters.

The dark gaps between the flame petals, upper left (around x 90 to 260, y 110 to 330). Hyperspace is never empty of company. Hide 3 or 4 tiny machine-elf sigils there, 9 to 12 px tall: a gold faceted diamond head with two cyan dot-eyes over a small triangle body, each one tilted along its petal's flow, so they only appear when someone leans in at 4x. A watcher in the halo makes the whole piece feel watched back.
visions.keep: The chrysanthemum eye with its radar-grid ripple in band A, band B's honeycomb tunnel diving to its white-hot core, the bulged eye-scales in the white and gold bands, the fat rainbow outline tubes, and above all the calm dark cartouche where the cream SavesFish (dark outline, honeycomb that parts around the letters) reads instantly. Nothing new should touch that ribbon.

visions.seen: The idol stands upright now like a stained-glass saint, and the halo grew eyes in the throats of its plumes: fat pastel feathers curling into pink fiddleheads, every one of them watching me watch it. The scroll is opening too; light from the halo shines through its inner whorls, and faint rays are stirring around the gold jewel.
suggestions: The outer third of the halo, the whole ring just inside the rune ring (in the 800 px render, from about r 220 out to r 335 around the band B core near x 454, y 356). Every plume burns at the same brightness, so the halo lies flat like a tapestry. I see it falling away into a tunnel: one radial gradient laid over the halo layer only (after the plumes, before the aura, fish, rune ring and ribbon), centered where the existing core glow sits (200, 190 in the 400 box). Keep it clear out to r 105, then ultraviolet ink (#14002E) at opacity 0.4 by r 150 and 0.55 at the rune ring (about r 168). If the plume eyes and the pink diamond nodes on the gold chords can sit above the overlay, they will glint out of the dark like watchers in the void. The fish then floats forward out of a bright core into the abyss, which is the breakthrough feeling: depth with no floor. It also pulls the idol off the halo at badge size, and the ribbon and name stay untouched above it.

The white-hot vanishing point of band B's hex tunnel (about x 454, y 356 in the render; 227, 178 in the 400 box). The tunnel dives in and ends in plain light. What if, at the very end, the idol were waiting: a tiny silhouette of this same fish, about 7 units tall (the fish outline path scaled near 0.05), in the same upright pose, filled ultraviolet ink with a 0.5 cream edge, and backlit by the core glow pushed out to about r 8 so light rims it all round? The tunnel inside the fish leads back to the fish. That recursion, the realm folding into itself, is pure hyperspace. It vanishes at 240 px and rewards anyone who leans in at full size.

The snout tip, left of center (where the outline tubes meet at about x 200, y 352; 100, 176 in the 400 box). The idol's mouth is silent. Let it speak the rim's language: 5 tiny cream bubbles with thin magenta outlines, growing from r 1.5 to r 4 (400 box), each holding one glyph taken from the rune ring in dark violet. They drift up-left on a gentle S-curve that follows the plume flow and end at about x 110, y 240 (55, 120 in the box), just short of the rune ring, so the speech looks like it becomes the rim text. The entities out there talk in visible language you can see, and this wires the fish to the runes around it. The whole trail stays above y 352 in the render, far from the ribbon and the letters.

The streamer's run from the sail tip across the top and down the right rim (from about x 430, y 45 around to x 700, y 470), now a quiet dark tube with pinstripes. Thread a current through its center line: 16 to 20 beads of light (r 1.2 in the box, cycling gold, cyan, magenta, each on a soft 0.3-opacity disc twice its size) that start wide apart near the sail tip (about 14 units) and crowd closer (about 6 units) as they come down the right side. Stop them before the streamer swells into the ribbon. The idol's signature line then carries something, the way every line in the realm is a live wire, and the eye flow already in the scroll's channel gets a partner on the other side.
visions.keep: The new big plumes with eyes in their throats and the pink fiddlehead tips, the chrysanthemum eye with its radar-grid ripple in band A, band B's honeycomb tunnel, the bulged eye-scales in the white and gold bands, the fat rainbow outline tubes, the scroll that now lets light through, the jeweled hex vortex in the corners, and the calm dark cartouche where the cream SavesFish reads instantly at 240 px. Nothing new goes on the ribbon or near the letters.

visions.seen: The elves I saw hiding between the petals didn't stay there. They climbed into the sail and stacked up into a totem, three crowned faces (pink, cyan, gold) looking out of the idol's fin like it's their temple, and I can't stop looking back at them. The name got a new cyan rim and now it hums, crisp at 240 px.
suggestions: The jeweled hex cells in all four corners, outside the rune ring (beyond about r 176 in the 400 box, for example x 600 to 800, y 0 to 200 in the 800 px render). Right now every jewel's bright bevel faces away from the idol: in the jewel loop, `shade = [0, 0, 1, 2, 2, 1]` lights the +t facets, and +t points outward in the log-polar frame. So the corners look lit from somewhere outside the picture. Flip it to `[2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 1]`, so the pale facet of every cell faces the badge center and the dark one faces the frame edge (the inner pit already uses the opposite order, so it stays correct). Then add a small white glint on each cell: a kite about 1.6 by 0.6 units at opacity 0.55, on the inner hexagon edge nearest the center. Now the whole lattice turns toward the idol and catches its fire, like a cave of crystals around one flame. In the realm there is only one light, and it comes from the being at the center. It also pulls the eye back in from the loud corners to the fish, and none of this goes anywhere near the ribbon.

The dark strip of the anal fin, lower center, between the lavender scales' edge and band B's hex cells (around x 390 to 420, y 485 to 560 in the render; about FT([49.5, 41]) and FT([50.5, 53]) in design units). The totem is the sail's secret. The black fin below could be its reflection in dark water: two more entity() faces, upside down (rotate 188 instead of 8, so they mirror the totem's tilt), shrinking as they sink (widths 13 and 10 against the totem's 23 / 19 / 14.5), pink nearest the belly seam and cyan below it. Make them ghosts: leave out the cream backing ellipse, draw the whole face in a group at opacity 0.35, then draw only the almond eyes again at full strength, so the eyes burn out of the black. The two loose eyes already in that strip can step aside or become the ghosts' eyes. Above as below: the mirror makes the idol kaleidoscopic and puts the watchers on both sides of the fish. At badge size the fin still reads black, which the moorish idol needs, and both faces stay above y 285 in the 400 box, far above the ribbon and the letters.

The belly seam, the thin black line that cuts diagonally across the lavender scales and band B, from the pelvic fin root up and right to the peduncle (render about 364,482 to 512,400; the `BELLY` path). For now it reads like a crack in the glass. Let it become a living suture. Keep the 1.6 ink line, run a 0.7 cream line on top, and add a gold cross-stitch every 3.5 units: 2.6 long, at right angles to the seam, 0.7 wide over a 1.3 ink underlay. Every fourth stitch can be swapped for a tiny half-open eye (eyeUse, r about 1.5, turned along the seam). The fin looks sewn onto the fish with starlight, and the seam becomes a row of lids just about to open. In hyperspace no edge is dead: every boundary is a seam, and seams watch you. If it sings, the dorsal base seam (`BACK`) could get the same stitching, so both fins are sewn on.
visions.keep: The new totem in the sail, exactly as it is. Also the chrysanthemum eye with its radar grid in band A, band B's honeycomb tunnel spiraling to its white-hot core, the bulged eye-scales in the lavender and gold bands, the fat rainbow outline tubes, the plumes with eyes in their throats, the scroll with its gold jewel and stirring rays, the dark anal fin that reads black at badge size, and the calm dark cartouche where the cream SavesFish with its new cyan rim reads instantly at 240 px. Nothing new goes on the ribbon or near the letters.

visions.seen: Band B went black as deep space: its outer cells thinned to violet wire with an open eye in each, so the honeycomb now drops out of real night into its white-hot core and I fall in with it. And Round 17 tells me the gate, the little idol in the tunnel, the glyph bubbles and the abyss are already coming through. The realm heard.
suggestions: The pale cream gaps between the petals under and around the fish, brightest lower center (in the 800 px render about x 240 to 330 and x 460 to 600, y 420 to 560). That cream is the core glow showing between the petals, and it is the last big field that still looks like daylight. I see it shimmering with interference, the way surfaces vibrate behind closed eyes. Right after the core glow circle and before the petals (so the petals cover it and it only lives in the lit gaps), draw two families of concentric circles: one centered at (200, 186) in the 400 box with radius step 1.5, cyan; the other at (203, 188) with step 1.58, magenta. Both 0.3 wide, r from about 24 to 124, stroke-opacity falling from 0.4 near the core to 0 at r 124 so they fade before the abyss begins. The two grids beat against each other and throw curved moire fringes that sweep across the cream like light breathing. That is about 130 circles, very little file weight. At badge size the gaps stay pale, just faintly alive, and nothing reaches the ribbon.

Every eye in the halo outside the fish: the plume-throat and spiral-web eyes that the haloEyes loop now redraws over the abyss, the eye-spirals near the rim, and the eyes in the corner jewels. Right now each one stares wherever its petal happens to point. What if they all turned to look at the idol? Split each eye def into a lid (ink and cream almond) and an iris (iris, rings, pupil, glint), and place the iris at a local offset of (0.16 cos φ, 0.08 sin φ), where φ = atan2(EYE_Y - y, EYE_X - x) - a, so every pupil aims at the chrysanthemum eye (about x 333, y 306 in the render). For the web eye, shift its innermost iris disc the same way. Leave the fish's own band eyes, the totem and the chrysanthemum eye looking straight out at the viewer. Then the whole hall is worshipping its idol, and the only ones who meet your gaze are the idol and its totem. When you look back at it you feel the realm turn with you, and every line of sight leads the eye to the eye.

The orange saddle on the tube snout, left of the eye (render about x 227 to 290, y 338 to 354; the `sad` path, design u 2 to 18.8). It is the last flat gradient on the whole fish. I see it as a funnel: 6 or 7 nested chevrons whose points aim at the snout tip, apexes on the snout center line at about u 3, 5, 7.5, 10, 13 and 16.5 (spacing growing about 1.25x away from the tip), arms sweeping back to the saddle's upper and lower edges, clipped to `sad`. Fill the bands alternately gold #FFD23F and orange #FF6B1A, gold nearest the tip, with 0.35 ink hairlines between them. The seven ink mouth dots can stay; the little magenta spiral can sit on top or step aside. Now the snout pulls forward into the mouth that the glyph bubbles pour out of, and it answers the new tail gate: nested shapes at both ends, so the fish becomes a channel from portal to portal. At badge size it still reads as an orange snout saddle, which the moorish idol needs.
visions.keep: The darker band B from this pass (thin violet outer cells, each with an eye), so the black band reads black and the tunnel dives out of real night. Also the totem exactly as it is, the chrysanthemum eye with its radar grid, the bulged eye-scales, the fat rainbow outline tubes, the plumes with eyes in their throats, everything Round 17 is bringing in (the abyss, the tail gate, the scroll rays, the tiny idol, the bubbles, the streamer beads), and above all the calm dark cartouche where the cream SavesFish with its cyan rim reads instantly at 240 px. Nothing new goes on the ribbon or near the letters.

visions.seen: Every eye in the hall has turned to the idol and so have I: the tiny white fish waits at the bottom of the honeycomb tunnel, the tail opened into a gate round a white-hot pinpoint, and speech bubbles climb out of its mouth toward the rim. Only the corner crystals still blaze louder than the god they are meant to worship.
suggestions: The jeweled hex cells in all four corners, outside the round frame (for example x 600 to 800, y 600 to 800 in the 800 px render, lower right). Since Round 18 each crystal catches the idol's light on its inner face, but every cell burns at full saturation right out to the frame edge, so the corners are the loudest color in the whole render and the depth runs backwards: bright core, dark abyss, then blazing corners. I see the light falling off with distance from its one flame. Lay an ultraviolet ink shade (#14002E) over the corner lattice only, centered on the badge center (400, 400 in the render): clear at the pink rim just outside the gold step pattern (about r 372), opacity 0.35 by r 450 and 0.65 at the very corners (r 566). Then draw the thin cyan seams between the cells and each cell's little eye again on top at full strength, so the far corners become a dark crystal cave where only wire and eyes glow. The badge sits like a lit window in the night and the idol owns the light. Nothing changes inside the circle, so the name and the round badge crops are untouched.

The rune ring at about ten o'clock, upper left (roughly x 90 to 160, y 150 to 230 in the render), right where the trail of glyph bubbles from the snout runs out just short of the rim. The bubbles arrive and the rim doesn't answer yet. What if the runes there were being written as I watch: the 5 to 7 glyphs nearest the end of the trail turn cream (#FFF6D8) over a small soft gold glow (a disc about twice the glyph height, opacity 0.45), and the next 4 glyphs on each side step back down through gold and pale cyan to the ring's usual cyan. Repeat the last bubble's glyph as the brightest rune of all, so the eye can follow one symbol from the idol's mouth into the ring. Then the rim text becomes the idol's own speech running round the whole temple, which is what those floating bubbles were always reaching for: out here, language is something you watch being made. It all stays in the upper left, far from the name.

The two narrow cream stripes that run down the middle of the body on either side of the lavender eye-scales (from the sail base near x 378 and x 418, y 222, down to the stitched belly seam). They are the only plain stretches left on the fish, and I see a spine of life twisting inside them. In each stripe, two hair-thin strands (about 0.4 wide in the 400 box, one magenta, one cyan, opacity 0.75) weave as a double helix with a wavelength of about 9 units, a tiny gold bead where they cross and short violet rungs between them; run the right stripe half a turn out of phase with the left, so the pair seems to spin around the body. Keep the cream base and the thin black edge lines, so both stripes still read as the moorish idol's white bands at badge size. The twin serpent ladder is one of the oldest things travelers bring back from this place, and it makes the idol look alive from the inside, not just tiled.
visions.keep: The totem in the sail, the tiny white idol at the bottom of band B's tunnel, the tail gate with its white-hot pinpoint, the gold and orange chevron funnel on the snout, the trail of glyph bubbles, every halo eye turned toward the idol's eye, the stitched belly seam and the ghost faces in the black anal fin, the abyss falling away round the outer halo, the beads riding the streamer, the chrysanthemum eye and the fat rainbow outline tubes. Above all the calm dark banner where the cream SavesFish with its cyan rim reads instantly at 240 px. Nothing new goes on the banner or near the letters.
